stem: An individual demonstrates normal hearing sensitivity on physical audio tests but struggles to interpret, organize, and comprehend speech in noisy environments. Which condition does this indicate?

options.text: Profound sensorineural hearing loss caused by inner-ear damage.
options.rationale: Sensorineural hearing loss involves measurable damage to the inner ear or auditory nerve, which shows up clearly on audiograms.

options.text: Conductive hearing loss caused by middle-ear blockages.
options.rationale: Conductive hearing loss is caused by physical blockages or damage in the outer or middle ear and reduces measurable sound volume.
CAPD is an impairment in how the brain analyzes and decodes auditory signals, occurring despite normal physical ear sensitivity.

options.text: Progressive presbycusis related to age-related hearing decline.
options.rationale: Presbycusis is age-related hearing deterioration characterized by measurable loss in detecting high-frequency sounds.

explanation: Central Auditory Processing Disorder (CAPD or APD) is a neurological condition where the ear senses sounds normally, but the brain has difficulty filtering, ordering, or understanding the incoming acoustic signals, particularly in busy or noisy environments.

references.title: American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA): Central Auditory Processing Disorder
